A second competent reading -- that CollisionAvoidance is an independently-initialized parallel region whose own local initial edge fully discharges its entry obligation -- remains compatible with the same exact facts and is not excluded by any explicit NL clause, so it survives as an undercutting defeater at the D1 boundary.

semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidance (and its collision_avoidance_deactive/active substates) must be reachable from the top-level initial entry so the always-on collision-avoidance safety behavior can execute alongside driving modes.

semantic_adjudication.reason: NL2 describes InitialState transitioning to HighwayMode or UrbanMode, implying independent top-level scopes, yet FinishState -- used from HighwayMode (line 15), AutonomousMode (line 40), and UrbanMode (line 43) -- has no explicit declaration and is assigned by first-mention convention to be a child of HighwayMode. This is an established containment fact from the exact source lines and closed model inventory. The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal notes the model is self-consistent and the divergence lies between author text and declaration semantics; this is a genuine competent alternative reading (the containment convention producing a technically consistent but NL-divergent structure) that survives as a rebutting-but-competing reading given the supplied source facts, rather than being excluded by any exact contrary containment declaration.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The closed model is internally self-consistent: it uniformly routes all cross-scope transitions (from AutonomousMode at line:40 and UrbanMode at line:43) into the single FinishState child of HighwayMode, so the divergence is only between the author's high-level NL description and the model-building/containment convention that assigns an undeclared state to its first-mention scope, not an internal structural defect within the closed model itself.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: FinishState's containment must follow the requirement's structure so that transitions from other scopes (AutonomousMode, UrbanMode) reach the same FinishState concept, not a copy routed exclusively through HighwayMode.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, cross-wrapper reachability, dead-end/frontier facts, stable termination, and bounded response. Deterministic facts show CollisionAvoidance and its two substates are structurally present (source-owned, satisfying containment) but the exact CollisionAvoidance composite has no incoming edge from the closed root/AutonomousMode hierarchy: inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts both mark state:CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active as reachable_from_initial=false, and both collision-avoidance events are declared but have zero reachable consumers. This is a distinct root-reachability defect (the owner scope is unreachable) plus a distinct event-consumer-coverage defect (declared consumers unreachable), separate from the owner-local initial_entry contract NL12-INITENTRY-1 (which is itself satisfied: [*]->collision_avoidance_deactive exists at transition:line:92/tr_0020) and separate from the two transition_endpoint contracts NL12-ENDPOINT-1/NL13-ENDPOINT-1 (whose exact edges exist at transition:line:93/94 but are unreachable). Also audited: FinishState termination (NL6-TERM-1, NL10-TERM-1) - FinishState has an outgoing edge FinishState->[*] triggered by enter_/urban_way_true/auto_finished_true with route-token effects that lead back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode/self-loop transitions (HighwayMode->HighwayMode, HighwayMode->UrbanMode), meaning the designated completion state is not stable and can route into continued operating behavior, violating stable termination. UnspecifiedInitial synthetic placeholders are compiler-owned and excluded from independent deadlock claims per protocol.

issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows reachable_from_initial=false for state:CollisionAvoidance:line:89, collision_avoidance_deactive:line:90, and collision_avoidance_active:line:91; verify_facts.non_proved contains matching refuted reachability checks; no transition in the complete 70-row transition inventory targets CollisionAvoidance or its substates from AutonomousMode, HighwayMode, UrbanMode, InitialState, or the root.
issues.reason: The NL text frames collision avoidance as a live behavior with declared events and responses that must actually occur during driving; the deterministic facts unanimously and independently (inspection-equivalent and verify) refute reachability of the entire scope from the model root, which is a structural gap distinct from the already-satisfied local initial edge and existing transition endpoints.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL does not explicitly state CollisionAvoidance must be entered from AutonomousMode's driving flow; it could be read as an independently-initialized parallel component whose own local [*]->collision_avoidance_deactive edge (present) is its only required entry, making global reachability out of scope for this NL segment.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance scope unreachable from model root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for the pedestrian/rear/front compound event; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify_facts.non_proved refuted check event-consumer:pedestrian_detected_...
issues.expected: The activation transition collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active must be reachable so that when the compound danger condition holds during operation, the system actually consumes the event and activates collision avoidance.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers declares the consumer transition:line:93 but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty; the EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic and the refuted verify_facts event-consumer check both confirm no reachable consumer exists because the owning composite is unreachable from root.
issues.reason: NL12 establishes an operational safety-response obligation (the system must actually transition when danger is detected), which is a stronger property than mere edge existence; declared-only consumer presence does not satisfy this reachable-response obligation per the frontier discipline on event-consumer coverage.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition edge itself exists exactly as required by the endpoint contract; one could argue declared existence discharges the NL obligation and unreachability is purely a root-reachability issue already captured separately.
issues.title: Collision-avoidance activation event has no reachable consumer

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for front_inactive_rear_inactive_pedestrian_inactive; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify_facts.non_proved refuted check event-consumer:front_inactive_rear_inactive_pedestrian_inactive.
issues.expected: The deactivation transition collision_avoidance_active -> collision_avoidance_deactive must be reachable so that when all danger conditions clear during operation, the system actually returns to the deactive state.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers declares the consumer transition:line:94 but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic and refuted verify_facts event-consumer check both confirm the absence of a reachable consumer.
issues.reason: NL13 states an operational return-to-safe-state obligation that requires the deactivation response to actually occur, which is a stronger reachable-consumer property than the endpoint-existence contract already satisfied; declaration alone is insufficient per frontier discipline.
issues.requirement_quote: Once in the collision_avoidance_active state, the collision avoidance system returns to the collision_avoidance_deactive state when there is no active danger, as indicated by the conditions `front_inactive`, `rear_inactive`, and `pedestrian_inactive`.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The exact edge exists as required by NL13-ENDPOINT-1's endpoint obligation; unreachability could be attributed entirely to the separate root-reachability defect rather than a distinct consumer-coverage violation.
issues.title: Collision-avoidance deactivation event has no reachable consumer

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions rows for transition:line:32 (FinishState->[*]/enter_), line:43 (FinishState->[*]/urban_way_true), line:48 (FinishState->[*]/auto_finished_true), combined with composite-level transitions transition:line:98 (HighwayMode->HighwayMode if R45RouteToken==5), line:100 (HighwayMode->UrbanMode if R45RouteToken==23), and line:103 (HighwayMode->HighwayMode if R45RouteToken==27), which are the resolved continuations of those route tokens.
issues.expected: FinishState must be a stable completion state for HighwayMode: once reached, the autonomous driving mode has formally ended and does not resume active driving behavior.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM gives FinishState outgoing transitions (FinishState -> [*] triggered by enter_, urban_way_true, and auto_finished_true, at transition:line:32/43/48) that exit back into HighwayMode's own [*]-collapse machinery, which the higher-level macro transitions HighwayMode->HighwayMode (R45RouteToken==5/27) and HighwayMode->UrbanMode (R45RouteToken==23) resolve into continued operating states (enter_hwy, or UrbanMode). Thus FinishState can route back into active driving behavior rather than remaining a stable end state.
issues.reason: Per the stable-termination frontier rule, every named completion state must be audited for exact target/active-ancestor continuations; here the closed-model FinishState has structural continuation paths back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode operating states via the composite-level route-token transitions, which is exactly the re-entrant/continued-behavior pattern the rule flags even though the FinishState->[*] edges themselves exist.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState
issues.strongest_rebuttal: These outgoing edges are compiler-generated macro-collapse artifacts representing PlantUML's history/self-loop encoding of composite-level events, not genuine authored continuations from FinishState; the source-level FinishState (line 41) has no explicit continuing transition in the PlantUML text, so this may be an artifact of the macro expansion rather than a real termination defect.
issues.title: FinishState is not a stable completion state; it re-enters continued operating behavior

issues.basis: Same evidentiary basis as the HighwayMode termination candidate: FinishState's outgoing transitions (line:32/43/48) and composite continuation transitions (line:98/100/103); exact_source_inventory tr_0026 (UrbanMode->FinishState).
issues.expected: FinishState must be a stable completion state for UrbanMode: once reached via auto_finished=true, the autonomous driving mode has formally ended and does not resume active driving.
issues.observed: The same FinishState node (contained in HighwayMode per source, targeted also from UrbanMode via tr_0026/transition:line:26 in the source model) has outgoing edges (transition:line:32/43/48) that route through the composite-level R45RouteToken transitions back into HighwayMode->HighwayMode/UrbanMode continuations, meaning UrbanMode's completion path also does not stably terminate.
issues.reason: NL10 independently asserts UrbanMode must terminate at FinishState; because both HighwayMode and UrbanMode share the identical non-terminating FinishState target, the same continuation defect applies to this separate contract's exact locus and must not be silently omitted merely because NL6-TERM-1 already reports it.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState once `auto_finished=true` is satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: This is the identical structural fact already raised for NL6-TERM-1 against the same FinishState node; since UrbanMode's completion also routes to the same FinishState, this may be considered a restatement rather than an independent structural defect specific to UrbanMode's path.
issues.title: FinishState (as UrbanMode's completion target) is not stable and re-enters operating behavior

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, cross-wrapper reachability, dead-end/frontier facts, stable termination, and bounded response. Deterministic facts show CollisionAvoidance and its two substates are structurally present (source-owned, satisfying containment) but the exact CollisionAvoidance composite has no incoming edge from the closed root/AutonomousMode hierarchy: inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts both mark state:CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active as reachable_from_initial=false, and both collision-avoidance events are declared but have zero reachable consumers. This is a distinct root-reachability defect (the owner scope is unreachable) plus a distinct event-consumer-coverage defect (declared consumers unreachable), separate from the owner-local initial_entry contract NL12-INITENTRY-1 (which is itself satisfied: [*]->collision_avoidance_deactive exists at transition:line:92/tr_0020) and separate from the two transition_endpoint contracts NL12-ENDPOINT-1/NL13-ENDPOINT-1 (whose exact edges exist at transition:line:93/94 but are unreachable). Also audited: FinishState termination (NL6-TERM-1, NL10-TERM-1) - FinishState has an outgoing edge FinishState->[*] triggered by enter_/urban_way_true/auto_finished_true with route-token effects that lead back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode/self-loop transitions (HighwayMode->HighwayMode, HighwayMode->UrbanMode), meaning the designated completion state is not stable and can route into continued operating behavior, violating stable termination. UnspecifiedInitial synthetic placeholders are compiler-owned and excluded from independent deadlock claims per protocol.
